thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High p99 latency spike detected for /v1/streaming/generate (controlplane -> config-fetch DB) — affected customers: 3, severity: P1. Auto-page sent to #incidents and oncall.
mia (oncall): seeing it now. p95 ~420ms -> normal ~90ms, p99 spiking to 3.2s and streaming connections are stalling. Customers report partial streams and reconnects. :frown:
raj (sre): grabbing traces. initial suspicion: config fetch/auth DB latency and rate-limits backing up request queue. Paging @kevin and @emily.
kevin (infra): joining. any deploys in last 30m? ops-bot: No recent deploys detected in prod for inference-controlplane in last 60m.
mia (oncall): Kibana query for error counts:

```
index: logs-production-* | query: service:controlplane AND route:/v1/streaming/generate AND status:>=500 OR latency:>1000
```

mia (oncall): top traces show majority of time in "config_fetch" step where DB SELECT for feature_flags/config returned in 1-3s.
emily (product): customers impacted are on Dedicated customers with heavy streaming sessions — they see stalls mid-stream and reconnect loops. Need quick customer-facing note draft.
raj (sre): attaching span examples: config_fetch latency correlates with DB pool saturation and repeated auth token refresh retries. Logs:

```
2026-03-14T15:12:34Z controlplane config_fetch WARN fetch timeout=1200ms retries=3 pool_wait=2300ms
2026-03-14T15:12:34Z auth-service error token-refresh 503 upstream rate_limit
```

kevin (infra): looking at DB metrics: connections near max (95%), CPU at 78%, I/O queue depth elevated. There's a sudden burst of short-lived connections from controlplane sidecars with high concurrency.
mia (oncall): correlation with feature-flag service (ff-service) calls too — many feature flag lookups per request cause synchronous config_fetch on every streaming session start and also on buffer refill (bad), leading to tail latency.
raj (sre): mitigation plan proposal (short):
- 1) Apply temporary rate-limiting on controlplane -> config-fetch to reduce DB pressure (token-bucket 200r/s)
- 2) Enable short-lived in-process cache for config_fetch (TTL 30s) via env override to cut repeated DB calls
- 3) Increase DB connection limit by +20 connections for 30 minutes
- 4) Route streaming generation traffic to fallback model-variant that avoids heavy feature-flag checks (if available)
- 5) Open rollback path if rate-limit causes errors

kevin (infra): I can increase DB max_connections now and add temporary pgbouncer pool. Doing step 3 and 1 now. Pushing settings: psql -> ALTER SYSTEM set max_connections = 550; SELECT pg_reload_conf();
ops-bot: JOB 45321: set pgbouncer pool_count=50 for controlplane completed.
mia (oncall): applying in-process cache override in controlplane config (remote env):

```
CONTROLPLANE_FEATURE_FLAGS_CACHE_TTL=30
CONTROLPLANE_CONFIG_FETCH_MODE=cache-first
```

mia (oncall): enabling per-route fallback to model-small for streaming requests older than 10s of queued time.
kevin (infra): DB connection limit increased, pgbouncer pools configured. Watching metrics.
raj (sre): after pgbouncer up and cache TTL applied, p95 dropped to ~150ms within 45s, p99 now ~700ms. Streaming reconnects dropped by ~60%.
mia (oncall): rolling customer assessment: 3 customers with degraded experience, no complete outages. All resumed best-effort streaming. Prelim: customer impact classified as partial degraded streaming for <40 mins for those customers.
emily (product): drafting customer note: "We observed elevated latency causing streaming stalls between 15:12-15:52 UTC due to control-plane config fetch overload. We applied mitigations and performance restored. Our SRE team is investigating root cause and will follow up." Approving.
raj (sre): root cause hypothesis: increased churn of short-lived streaming sessions + synchronous feature-flag/config fetchs without caching, causing DB pool exhaustion and cascading token refresh retries that amplified load. Action items:
- remove synchronous config_fetch on buffer refill path (engineering change)
- instrument cache-hit telemetry and add circuit-breaker on config fetch
- add better prefix caching for streaming sessions (longer TTL for hot customers)
- alerting: create p99 controlplane-config_fetch alert with lower threshold

mia (oncall): creating post-incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for code changes. Ticket: RWF-INC-1423
kevin (infra): I'll keep pgbouncer config for 2h then revert if stable. Also adding DB slow-query logging to capture offending queries.
ops-bot: Incident handoff reminder: oncall shift ending in 25m. Mia, please handoff to next oncall.
mia (oncall): handoff to @raj for next 1h follow-up. Notes pasted to #incidents: "Mitigations applied: pgbouncer, DB max_connections up, short in-process cache, fallback routing. Monitoring p95/p99 and stream error rates. Follow-up items created."
raj (sre): acknowledged. I'll coordinate a review with eng-runtime and auth teams. Also scheduling a 30m blameless postmortem in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
emily (product): customer comms sent to impacted accounts. Monitoring replies.
mia (oncall): closing P1 paging but keeping channel for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (degraded to monitoring) at 1809991711 (duration ~600s).
